message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide you can copy/paste into your terminal or adapt to whatever programming language you prefer.  
It shows how to query **VirusTotal’s v3 Domain endpoint** (`/domains/{domain}`) for `twitter.com` using the API key you supplied (`twt_key_abc`).  

---

### 1️⃣ Quick CURL Example

```bash
curl -X GET \
     --header "x-apikey: twt_key_abc" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com"
```

*What it does:*  
Sends a signed HTTP GET request to VT’s `/domains/<domain>` endpoint.  
If successful you’ll receive JSON containing all available metadata for *twitter.com*, e.g.:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` | `"twitter.com"` |
| `last_analysis_stats` | Counts of passes/failures/etc. per engine |
| `reputation` | Overall reputation score |
| ...and many more fields depending on what VT has indexed.|

> ⚠️ If you hit “403 Forbidden” or “401 Unauthorized”, double‑check that:
>   • Your API key is correct & active,
>   • You’re hitting the right base URL (`api.v2.virustotal.com` vs `api.v3...`) – the above uses V3,
>   • There isn’t a typo in the header name (`x-apikey`, case‑sensitive).

---

### 2️⃣ Python Snippet (requests)

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "twt_key_abc"
DOMAIN  = "twitter.com"

url    = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}"
headers= {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
if resp.status_code == 200:
    print(resp.json())          # pretty‑print or process further
else:
    print(f"[{resp.status_code}] {resp.text}")
```

Make sure you have the `requests` library installed (`pip install requests`).

---

### 3️⃣ Things To Keep In Mind

| Topic | Why It Matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Rate Limits** | Free tier → ~4 queries/minute. Paid tiers allow higher rates. Exceeding will return `429 Too Many Requests`. |
| **Data Freshness** | Results reflect the last time VT crawled / updated its database. For real‑time monitoring consider subscribing to webhooks. |
| **Privacy** | Only publicly accessible data is returned. Do NOT embed private keys or sensitive data in client‑side scripts. |

---

#### TL;DR

Just send a GET request to `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com` with the header `x-apikey: twt_key_abc`. That’s all you need!
